paragraphs: Some optimization algorithms spend much of their effort asking another system for exact information. When that system is a complex model or database, each answer can be expensive. This paper studies how a faster, less reliable source of information can reduce that expense when computing a maximum-weight basis of a matroid, a structure that captures many combinatorial optimization problems.

The algorithms can consult both a precise “clean” oracle and an imprecise “dirty” oracle. They use the dirty oracle to help make progress while reserving clean queries for resolving uncertainty. The analysis connects the number of clean queries to the quality of the dirty oracle, so better approximate information can translate into less expensive verification.

The guarantees also address poor advice: even arbitrarily inaccurate dirty oracles do not destroy robustness, with performance approaching that of classical algorithms. The authors prove that their algorithms are best possible in several respects and outline extensions to additional oracle types, dirty queries that have a cost, and other matroid problems.
neurips-2024-accelerating-matroid-optimi.tldr: Fast, imperfect information can reduce expensive exact queries in matroid optimization while preserving robustness when that information is poor.

paragraphs: Convex-concave minimax optimization involves choosing one set of variables to minimize an objective while another set maximizes it. This paper develops second-order methods for these problems that achieve an optimal convergence rate while adapting their step sizes. The practical motivation is to use curvature information without repeatedly searching for an acceptable step.

The methods combine optimistic updates with second-order information. Their step size is defined recursively using the gradient norm and the prediction error in the optimistic update. Each iteration requires solving just one linear system, and the update avoids line search and backtracking. This makes adaptation part of the update rule itself rather than a separate sequence of trial steps.

The theoretical guarantees distinguish two settings. One version needs the Lipschitz constant governing changes in the Hessian. With the additional assumption that gradients are Lipschitz continuous, a parameter-free version estimates that constant locally while keeping iterates bounded. The paper also compares practical performance with existing second-order minimax algorithms, complementing its convergence analysis.
neurips-2024-adaptive-and-optimal-second.tldr: Adaptive second-order minimax algorithms achieve optimal convergence rates with one linear solve per iteration and no line search.

paragraphs: AuctionNet provides a research environment for studying bidding decisions in large advertising auctions. It addresses the difficulty of accessing realistic large-scale games by combining an auction simulator, a substantial generated dataset, and evaluations of baseline bidding algorithms. Its design draws on a real online advertising platform.

The environment separates the auction process into interacting modules. Deep generative networks produce advertising opportunities intended to resemble real data while reducing sensitive-data exposure risks. A bidding module supplies varied automated agents trained with different algorithms. The auction mechanism uses Generalized Second Price as its foundation, while allowing researchers to customize the rules.

The released dataset contains 10 million advertising opportunities, 48 automated bidding agents, and more than 500 million auction records. Evaluations cover approaches including linear programming, reinforcement learning, and generative models. AuctionNet also supported a competition with over 1,500 teams. Together, these components provide a common setting for comparing bidding strategies; the authors additionally suggest its usefulness for broader research on decision-making in large games.
neurips-2024-auctionnet-a-novel-benchmar.tldr: AuctionNet combines a realistic advertising-auction environment, large generated dataset, and baseline evaluations for studying automated bidding.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can generate convincing outputs yet struggle to satisfy demanding constraints. Trust sampling addresses this during generation without additional training. It treats loss-guided diffusion as a sequence of constrained optimization problems, aiming to balance the model's existing generative behavior with instructions expressed through a constraint-related loss.

At each diffusion level, the method allows multiple gradient steps on a proxy for the desired constraint. It stops trusting that proxy according to the variance at the current level. This makes the amount of guidance depend on the stage of generation, rather than applying an unrestricted sequence of optimization steps.

A second safeguard estimates the diffusion model's state manifold, representing the states associated with its generation process. Optimization can terminate early when a sample begins to move away from that manifold. Together, the two controls regulate how far constraint guidance can push a sample. Experiments on images and 3D motion report significant generation-quality improvements over existing methods, supporting the approach across substantially different output domains.
neurips-2024-constrained-diffusion-with-.tldr: Trust sampling improves constrained diffusion generation by taking guidance steps only while the constraint proxy and model-state estimates support them.

paragraphs: Multi-distribution learning seeks a single predictor that performs well across several data distributions, using training samples from each. For binary losses and hypothesis classes with finite VC dimension, existing approaches achieve nearly optimal sample requirements. Their computational efficiency assumes access to an efficient empirical risk minimizer, which finds a good predictor for observed training data.

However, those approaches produce randomized predictors. The paper asks whether their randomness can be removed while retaining useful guarantees across all distributions. This differs from classical PAC learning, where deterministic predictors can already achieve optimal sample complexity. The distinction matters because efficient training does not automatically imply efficient conversion to a deterministic decision rule.

The authors establish a computational barrier through a reduction to discrepancy minimization: derandomization can be hard even when empirical risk minimization is efficient. They also identify a structural condition under which conversion is possible through an efficient black-box procedure. The result separates the general difficulty from a setting where existing randomized predictors can be systematically made deterministic.
neurips-2024-derandomizing-multi-distrib.tldr: Removing randomness from multi-distribution predictors can be computationally hard, but a structural condition enables efficient conversion.

paragraphs: Conditional generative modeling aims to produce samples that agree with specified conditioning information. This paper studies that task through conditional optimal transport, which describes how to couple source and target distributions while respecting the conditional structure. Its theoretical contribution is a dynamic formulation that extends the Benamou-Brenier theorem to this setting.

The formulation supports a simulation-free method based on flows. The method first connects an arbitrary source distribution to the specified target through a triangular conditional transport plan. It then learns to approximate the geodesic path of distributions induced by that plan. In this construction, the transport plan determines the route through distribution space that the conditional generator approximates.

Both the theory and the method apply in infinite-dimensional settings, making the approach relevant to a broad class of Bayesian inverse problems. The experiments include such an inverse problem alongside other challenging conditional generation tasks. The reported outcome is competitive performance, supporting the proposed connection between transport geometry and practical conditional generation without claiming universal superiority.
neurips-2024-dynamic-conditional-optimal.tldr: A dynamic theory of conditional optimal transport yields a simulation-free generative method that also applies to infinite-dimensional inverse problems.

paragraphs: A Lyapunov function can provide a mathematical certificate of a dynamical system's global stability. Discovering such a function is a longstanding challenge: there is no known general solution, and algorithmic solvers cover only some small polynomial systems. This paper investigates whether symbolic transformers can help discover these certificates.

The central contribution is a way to generate synthetic training examples from randomly generated solutions. This supplies examples for training sequence-to-sequence transformers on the discovery task. The approach makes training-data construction a key part of the method, using available solutions as the starting point for producing examples of the mathematical relationship the model should learn.

The authors report that transformers trained on these datasets outperform algorithmic solvers and humans on the polynomial systems they study. They also report discovering new Lyapunov functions for non-polynomial systems, extending the demonstrated use beyond the setting covered by existing solvers. These results show progress on function discovery for evaluated systems; the paper's stated lack of a general solution remains the broader mathematical context.
neurips-2024-global-lyapunov-functions-a.tldr: Transformers trained on synthetic examples discover Lyapunov functions, outperforming compared solvers and humans on studied polynomial systems.

paragraphs: GMAI-MMBench evaluates how well large vision-language models handle a broad range of medical questions. The paper argues that existing benchmarks often concentrate on a single domain and provide too little variation in the detail being assessed. Its goal is to make medical evaluation more comprehensive and more closely connected to varied clinical tasks.

The benchmark brings together 284 datasets spanning 38 medical image modalities, 18 clinically related tasks, and 18 departments. It uses visual question answering and covers four levels of perceptual granularity. A lexical tree organizes the content so users can customize evaluation tasks, making it possible to assess different combinations of medical content and perceptual detail.

The authors evaluate 50 vision-language models. GPT-4o achieves 53.96% accuracy, illustrating substantial remaining difficulty on this benchmark even for an advanced model. They also identify five areas of insufficiency in current models. The contribution is therefore both a broad assessment resource and evidence of weaknesses that further medical-model development needs to address.
neurips-2024-gmai-mmbench-a-comprehensiv.tldr: GMAI-MMBench evaluates medical vision-language models across diverse tasks and image types, revealing substantial room for improvement.

paragraphs: Understanding extreme climate events requires examining how relevant physical variables change across both space and time. This is difficult because an event can follow its drivers after a delay, and the spatial response can vary from place to place. The paper introduces a learning approach and benchmarks for identifying these relationships.

The network jointly predicts extreme events and the locations and times of potential drivers in the input variables. Its crucial design constraint is that predictions of extremes must come from binary masks marking the identified drivers. This connects the identification task directly to event prediction, requiring the selected patterns to carry information useful for predicting extremes.

The authors report that this design successfully identifies drivers correlated with extreme events. That finding concerns predictive association rather than establishing causal effects. Evaluation uses three newly created synthetic benchmarks, including two based on remote sensing or reanalysis climate data, plus two real reanalysis datasets. Public code and datasets provide resources for studying this difficult spatial and temporal identification problem.
neurips-2024-identifying-spatio-temporal.tldr: A network predicts climate extremes through masks of candidate drivers, identifying spatial and temporal patterns correlated with those events.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation assigns a category to each image pixel. When a model encounters an unfamiliar domain, changes in urban appearance and environmental style can undermine its predictions, even when it uses a vision foundation model. This paper targets the challenge of preserving scene understanding across those changes.

The proposed Frequency-Adapted learning scheme, FADA, uses a Haar wavelet transformation to separate frequency components. Its approach treats low-frequency information as carrying scene content and high-frequency information as carrying style. Frequency tokens handle these components separately throughout learning, giving the model distinct ways to process content and variation in appearance.

FADA has two branches: the low-frequency branch stabilizes scene content, while the high-frequency branch learns styles and removes their influence on domain-generalized segmentation. The authors report state-of-the-art results across the evaluated segmentation settings and compatibility with several vision foundation models. These findings support frequency-based adaptation as a way to make use of foundation-model representations when the deployment domain looks different from the training domain.
neurips-2024-learning-frequency-adapted-.tldr: FADA separates content and style into frequency branches to improve vision foundation models' segmentation on unseen domains.

paragraphs: Spatiotemporal data can contain many missing observations across locations and times. Existing imputation methods often pass information repeatedly through spatial and temporal connections. The paper's analysis finds that these iterative models are sensitive both to missing data and to sparse graph connections, helping explain unstable performance across datasets.

The proposed One-step Propagation and Confidence-based Refinement method, OPCR, first uses sparse attention to spread available observations directly into a global context. This produces initial spatial and temporal imputations without repeated propagation. The authors' theoretical analysis attributes the sparsity dependence of these one-step modules to data sparsity alone, addressing the additional sensitivity to graph sparsity identified for iterative methods.

OPCR then estimates confidence by relating missing entries to valid observations. It uses that confidence and spatiotemporal dependencies to refine the separate initial estimates. This second stage gives the method a way to distinguish estimates according to their support in observed data. Experiments across downstream tasks with highly sparse inputs report better effectiveness and robustness than state-of-the-art imputation methods.
neurips-2024-learning-from-highly-sparse.tldr: OPCR fills sparse spatiotemporal data through direct propagation followed by confidence-based refinement, improving reported imputation effectiveness and robustness.

paragraphs: Entropic optimal transport connects source and target distributions subject to constraints on their marginals. Strict matching can create problems when outliers or class imbalances are present. Unbalanced entropic optimal transport relaxes those constraints to mitigate these issues, but existing continuous solvers can rely on heuristics or complicated objectives involving several neural networks.

This paper proposes a lightweight solver with theoretical justification. Its central step is a new optimization view that yields a tractable objective without a minimax structure. Combining this objective with a lightweight parameterization produces a method intended to be simpler and faster to optimize than the more elaborate alternatives described in the paper.

The authors report solving continuous unbalanced transport problems in minutes on a CPU and provide illustrative performance examples. They also prove universal approximation of unbalanced transport solutions and establish generalization bounds. These results address complementary questions: whether the solver can represent the desired solutions, how learning relates to generalization, and whether the resulting computation can be practical.
neurips-2024-light-unbalanced-optimal-tr.tldr: A lightweight, theoretically justified objective makes continuous unbalanced entropic optimal transport practical to solve in minutes on a CPU.

paragraphs: LiDAR measurements differ across sensors, vehicles, and driving environments. Those differences make it difficult to reuse data or perception models across datasets. LiDAR Translator, or LiT, tackles this by translating the data between domains, supporting both adaptation to another domain and joint learning from several domains.

The framework combines scene reconstruction with sensor modeling. One module reconstructs foreground objects and background structure. Another statistically models LiDAR rays and simulates ray-drop, accounting for measurements that are absent from the observed scan. A hardware-accelerated ray-casting engine makes the translation process fast. Together, these components address both the scene being measured and the way a sensor samples it.

The authors report state-of-the-art zero-shot and unified-domain detection across diverse LiDAR datasets. These results support direct data translation as a route toward sharing information across otherwise mismatched domains. The contribution is a framework that connects scene geometry, sensor behavior, and efficient simulation to improve the use of heterogeneous LiDAR data for autonomous-driving perception.
neurips-2024-lit-unifying-lidar-language.tldr: LiT translates LiDAR data across domains using scene reconstruction and sensor simulation, improving cross-domain and unified detection.

paragraphs: MonkeySee uses a convolutional neural network to reconstruct naturalistic images directly from macaque brain activity. The study examines neuronal populations in V1, V4, and IT, extending its decoding analysis from lower-level to higher-level visual signals. The reconstructed images provide a way to study how information in those populations can be translated into pixels.

The authors report high-precision reconstructions and distinct readout characteristics across the three brain areas. Comparing the outputs therefore serves more than the goal of reproducing an image: it also examines differences in what the decoder can extract from different neural populations. The work expands the use of CNN-based decoding across these levels of visual representation.

A space-time-resolved decoding technique adds temporal detail to the analysis, allowing the reconstruction process to inform understanding of neural representations over time. The model also includes a learned receptive field layer that helps reveal how it processes data during training. Together, these additions make the decoder a tool for both image reconstruction and interpretation of the learned readout.
neurips-2024-monkeysee-space-time-resolv.tldr: MonkeySee reconstructs naturalistic images from macaque visual brain signals and uses spatial and temporal decoding to examine neural representations.

paragraphs: Sparse mixture-of-experts models increase capacity while activating only part of the model for a given input. However, too few experts may receive optimization activity, limiting how effectively the model learns to use a larger expert collection. This paper proposes Multi-Head Mixture-of-Experts, or MH-MoE, to improve expert activation.

MH-MoE divides each input token into several sub-tokens. These are routed to a diverse set of experts for parallel processing and then combined back into the original token form. This gives different experts access to different parts of a token's representation, increasing expert participation while bringing together information from multiple representation spaces.

The authors describe the mechanism as straightforward to implement and compatible with other sparse mixture-of-experts frameworks. Experiments span models from 300 million to 7 billion parameters, covering English language modeling, multilingual language modeling, and masked multimodal modeling, alongside downstream evaluations. The reported results support the effectiveness of the approach across these settings, connecting increased expert activation with improved use of model capacity.
neurips-2024-multi-head-mixture-of-exper.tldr: MH-MoE splits tokens across multiple experts and recombines them, increasing expert activation and improving performance across evaluated modeling tasks.

paragraphs: Point cloud interpolation estimates intermediate 3D observations from measurements taken at different times. Sparse points and complex non-rigid motion make this difficult. NeuroGauss4D-PCI addresses the problem by combining a structured geometric representation of changing point clouds with learned features that depend on both position and time.

The method first uses iterative soft clustering to organize points into Gaussian clouds. A temporal radial basis function component interpolates Gaussian parameters smoothly and captures temporal residuals. A four-dimensional Gaussian deformation field then tracks how those parameters evolve, providing a continuous representation of spatial and temporal deformation.

Alongside this geometric description, a neural field maps coordinates x, y, z, and time into higher-dimensional features. The model adaptively fuses those learned features with the Gaussian deformation features. The authors report leading interpolation performance on the object-level DHB dataset and the larger autonomous-driving NL-Drive dataset. They also describe scalability to automatic labeling and point cloud densification, extending the potential use of the combined representation beyond intermediate-frame generation.
neurips-2024-neurogauss4d-pci-4d-neural-.tldr: NeuroGauss4D-PCI combines Gaussian deformation fields and neural fields to improve interpolation of sparse, dynamically changing point clouds.

paragraphs: Quantization compresses numerical information used in machine learning, including gradients, weights, activations, and datasets. Adaptive quantization chooses a representation to minimize error for the actual input. That focus can improve accuracy relative to optimizing for a worst-case input, but finding optimal adaptive solutions has been viewed as too demanding in time and memory.

This paper revisits Adaptive Stochastic Quantization and develops algorithms that still find optimal solutions while improving the asymptotic time and space requirements. The contribution addresses the computational cost of obtaining the optimum. It therefore targets a barrier to using input-specific quantization in applications where the numerical data being compressed can vary.

The authors also introduce a faster approximation algorithm for large inputs that need to be quantized on the fly. This provides an additional option when runtime matters more than exact optimality. Their experiments suggest that the improved algorithms may enable wider use of adaptive stochastic quantization in machine learning, while retaining that broader adoption as a possibility supported by the results.
neurips-2024-optimal-and-approximate-ada.tldr: Improved exact and approximate algorithms reduce the computational barriers to adaptive stochastic quantization.

paragraphs: OxonFair is an open-source toolkit for enforcing fairness constraints in binary classification. It supports tabular data, language tasks, and computer vision classification. The toolkit jointly optimizes a performance objective and fairness requirements, aiming to limit the performance loss that can accompany enforcing a chosen fairness constraint.

Its measures can be built from true positives, false positives, false negatives, and true negatives. That flexibility makes the toolkit extensible and lets it express all the decision-based group metrics covered by two review articles discussed in the paper. Fairness can also be enforced using validation data, which the authors describe as providing robustness to a range of overfitting challenges.

The paper reports that joint optimization can even improve performance when the unfair baseline is inadequately tuned. This is a qualified finding about those baselines, alongside the broader aim of minimizing degradation. Compatibility with sklearn, Autogluon, and PyTorch makes the approach usable with established machine-learning workflows, bringing varied fairness objectives into a shared practical toolkit.
neurips-2024-oxonfair-a-flexible-toolkit.tldr: OxonFair jointly optimizes classification performance and flexible fairness constraints across tabular, language, and vision tasks.

paragraphs: Neural-network architectures and loss functions often contain parameter symmetries, so movement in some parameter directions can leave the modeled objective unchanged. This paper examines how stochastic gradient descent interacts with exponential symmetries, a broad subclass of continuous symmetries. Its focus is the role of gradient noise in shaping motion along those directions.

The authors prove that this noise creates a systematic parameter motion, termed a Noether flow, along a degenerate direction toward a unique fixed point independent of initialization. They call that point a noise equilibrium because noise contributions from different directions become balanced and aligned there. The result gives noise a structured role in learning dynamics within the symmetry setting studied.

The paper then shows how balancing and aligning gradient noise can provide an alternative mechanism for explaining progressive sharpening or flattening and the formation of representations. It also connects this perspective to representation normalization and warmup. These implications offer a way to interpret training behavior through the interaction of parameter symmetry and stochastic updates.
neurips-2024-parameter-symmetry-and-nois.tldr: For exponential parameter symmetries, SGD noise drives a systematic flow toward a noise equilibrium, offering explanations for several training phenomena.

paragraphs: BiXT is a Transformer architecture designed to process longer sequences while scaling computation and memory linearly with input size. It draws on Perceiver architectures and addresses a bottleneck in how input tokens exchange information with latent variables. The goal is efficient processing that still supports varied modalities and prediction tasks.

Its central module uses bidirectional cross-attention: input tokens and latent variables attend to one another simultaneously, using an attention symmetry that emerges between them. Across layers, this allows information about what is present and where it is located to develop together. That combination supports tasks requiring detailed spatial predictions as well as predictions about whole instances.

Experiments cover point cloud part segmentation, image segmentation and classification, hierarchical sequence modeling, and document retrieval. The authors report outperforming larger competitors on vision tasks by using longer sequences efficiently. They also report matching full Transformer variants on sequence modeling and retrieval, with 28% fewer floating-point operations and speedups of up to 8.4 times in the reported comparisons.
neurips-2024-perceiving-longer-sequences.tldr: BiXT uses simultaneous bidirectional cross-attention to process longer sequences efficiently while retaining competitive performance across modalities.

paragraphs: Message-passing graph neural networks combine information from neighboring entities through an aggregation module. Simple summation has strong theoretical guarantees about distinguishing inputs, yet practitioners often prefer more elaborate aggregators. This paper proposes a possible explanation: summation may inadequately mix features originating from different neighbors for the downstream task.

Sequential Signal Mixing Aggregation, or SSMA, changes how those neighbor features are combined. It treats each neighbor's features as a two-dimensional discrete signal and sequentially convolves the signals. This explicitly mixes information across neighbors within the aggregation operation. The method is designed as a plug-in component for existing message-passing architectures.

The authors evaluate SSMA with established graph neural networks and report substantial gains across several benchmarks, including state-of-the-art results in many settings. These experiments support the usefulness of the proposed aggregation mechanism. The broader explanation remains framed as a possible account of the gap between summation's theoretical strengths and the practical success of richer aggregators: distinguishing neighborhoods and combining their features usefully are related but different concerns.
neurips-2024-sequential-signal-mixing-ag.tldr: SSMA mixes neighboring graph features through sequential convolutions, improving established message-passing networks across evaluated benchmarks.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation classifiers often compare each pixel's features with fixed category prototypes learned during training. This can struggle when pixels from the same category look different across images. It can also underuse the spatial structure of objects, contributing to blurry boundaries and weak recognition of fine details.

SSA-Seg adapts those prototypes to the image being processed. It first obtains coarse masks using the fixed prototypes, then uses the masks to guide adjustments toward the image's semantic and spatial centers. Classification considers both kinds of adapted prototypes together, incorporating category appearance and spatial organization into the final pixel decisions.

The paper also introduces online multi-domain distillation to improve this adaptation process. Experiments on three public benchmarks report significant segmentation improvements over baseline models with only a small increase in computation. The findings support adapting the classifier itself to the test image as a practical way to address variation within categories and make better use of object structure during segmentation.
neurips-2024-ssa-seg-semantic-and-spatia.tldr: SSA-Seg adapts category prototypes to each image's semantic and spatial structure, improving segmentation with little additional computation.

paragraphs: This paper studies two-layer ReLU networks for one-dimensional nonparametric regression with noisy labels. In this setting, kernels are provably suboptimal and fitting every training label does not yield benign overfitting. The authors therefore analyze local minima to which constant-learning-rate gradient descent can converge stably, rather than focusing on zero-training-loss solutions.

They show that such stable minima represent functions whose weighted first-order total variation is bounded. The bound depends on the inverse learning rate, label noise, and error against the true function. This links optimization stability to control over function variation: the learning rate constrains the kinds of fitted functions that can occur at stable minima.

Under mild assumptions, the paper also proves a nearly optimal mean squared error rate of n to the power of minus four-fifths, up to logarithmic factors, strictly inside the data support. Simulations show large learning rates producing sparse linear spline fits. Together, these results connect stable training to generalization without explicit regularization in this specific regression setting.
neurips-2024-stable-minima-cannot-overfi.tldr: For noisy one-dimensional regression, stability under fixed-step gradient descent constrains ReLU fits and yields near-optimal generalization under stated assumptions.

paragraphs: Post-training quantization reduces the numerical precision of an already trained model, helping make very large generative models more practical to deploy on edge devices. However, quantization itself can require substantial time and resources. That expense becomes especially relevant when models are updated frequently or many hyperparameter settings must be tried.

The paper proposes aespa to balance quantization accuracy and efficiency. Its key choice is to quantize one layer at a time while measuring reconstruction at the attention-module level. This lets the computation retain the efficiency of layer-wise processing while accounting for dependencies across layers within attention, which the authors identify as a weakness of existing learning-free approaches.

Experiments on several language models and an analysis of computational complexity support the authors' claim that aespa is both accurate and efficient. The method's significance lies in connecting the unit of efficient computation with a broader reconstruction target. It addresses interactions inside Transformer attention without requiring the quantization process to treat every layer as an isolated accuracy problem.
neurips-2024-towards-next-level-post-tra.tldr: aespa combines layer-wise quantization with attention-level reconstruction to balance Transformer quantization accuracy and computational cost.

paragraphs: Adapting a segmentation model between ordinary image domains does not fully address transfer to depth, infrared, or event data. These modalities differ substantially in how they represent a scene. MADM uses a text-to-image diffusion model pretrained on image-text pairs to improve unsupervised segmentation adaptation across these larger modality gaps.

One component targets unreliable pseudo-labels, which are model-generated labels used to guide adaptation. Transferring labels from one modality to another can sharply reduce their accuracy. MADM introduces latent noise into diffusion-based pseudo-label generation to stabilize these labels and improve their accuracy, addressing the quality of the supervision used during adaptation.

A complementary component addresses the low resolution of diffusion-model latent features. It converts category labels into RGB colors through a palette and regresses those representations in latent space, allowing the pretrained decoder to upsample them into finer-grained features. Experiments report state-of-the-art adaptation from images to depth, infrared, and event modalities. The two components jointly address label reliability and the spatial detail needed for pixel-level predictions.
neurips-2024-unsupervised-modality-adapt.tldr: MADM uses diffusion-based pseudo-labels and latent label reconstruction to improve unsupervised segmentation transfer from images to other visual modalities.
